# introduction
Read the guidelines at .github/copilot-instructions. You have the role of reviewer, you will write plans for analyzer and then start an analyzer subagent to carry out that those plans. It is up to you how to schedule and send off the tasks to analyzer subagent(s), but keep the work of each subagent isolated. Be careful of recompiling executables which might be in use by another program. If there is a chance a file is being edited or executable ran or will soon-to-be ran by anther subagent, then wait until that subagent's task has concluded. For analysis production use 20-30 threads, for skimming use 5 threads for mc and 10 threads for data.


# track selection systematics rules 
Enforce the new rule on systematic track residual corrections. There is some ambiguity between which systematic conditions are applied on the reco set or on both the reco and gen sets when the correction is calculated. Enfore the following behaviors in the runner scripts now and hard code them now for both pp and pPb cases.
Apply variation condition on both reco and gen level MC:
 - muon-track rejection, weather isMuTagged or trackMuDR is used, the same track cut should be applied to both mc reco and gen. Implement the same format as rejectMuonMatchedTrack in the main analysis. This is applied at the track selection level.
Apply condition only to reco MC:
 - track selection loose/tight, applied when selecting the loose / nominal / tight tree from the skim root file. 
 - track correction weight variation, applied when we scale the track weight up or down by 0.976 or 1.024.
Applied to neither reco or mc:
 - pile-up (only applied to data), but we still calculate the track residuals since the VZ and Z weights induce new track weights
 - ScaleFactor (only applied to data), no residual corrections
 - energy extrapolation, no residual since energy weight calculate post-track residual.
Apply these but do not rerun track residuals at this time. Return with a report for which systematics this affects, if any.

# propagation of test < 15 GeV correction factors
Propagate the test residual corrections for nominal and muon-track residual cases where we require < 15 GeV max track pT bin. Make a test muon-track standalone systematics comparing the two. Along the way you will need to calculate a test energy extrapolation as well. Generally just follow the direction in 20260411-5.md.


# conclusion
Make the minimum number of edits necessary to implement functionality. Do not add superflous error statement catches or checks. 

Have the subanalyzer handoff a summary to you and you should review that summary for flaws. Update copilot instructions on the new norms detailed here and learned by you or the subanalyzer throught these tasks.
